dump.name: gtfo-inspection/dumper/dump.cs
dump.note: Local read-only copy used for this audit. dump.cs records the short type name, the il2cpp RVA and the exact parameter list.

used.name: Modules-ASM.dll
used.readWith: Mono.Cecil metadata reading (member kinds, field offsets and enum constants only)

used.name: GlobalFramework-ASM.dll
used.readWith: Mono.Cecil metadata reading; holds Globals.Global, which carries the static rundown id the policy activates on

question: Can a package replace the equipment a player may choose from — and the equipment the game equips by itself — without writing the game's own data or the player's saved file?

answer.hook: Two hooks and no data write. `Gear.GearManager.GetAllGearForSlot` postfix at `HarmonyPriority.Last` projects the array the picker is built from, and `Gear.GearManager.OnGearLoadingDone` prefix at `HarmonyPriority.First` narrows the three pool lists in place before `RescanFavorites` reads them.
answer.whyTwo: `GetAllGearForSlot` is the only source of a slot's selectable gear, so the postfix covers every consumer of the list at once, but a gear the game equips by itself is named by the player's saved favorites file rather than chosen from that list: narrowing the pool before `RescanFavorites` runs is what makes a saved vanilla name match nothing and fall back to the same pool's first entry.
answer.activation: `Globals.Global.get_RundownIdToLoad()`. A policy file is only in force for the rundown it names.
answer.discovery: `BepInEx/plugins/<exactly one directory>/forge/loadout.json`, read once during plugin Load.
answer.identity: Either the record text `Gear.GearIDRange.get_PlayfabItemInstanceId` holds — `OfflineGear_ID_<canonical decimal>`, the same spelling the `gear-block` mount uses — or `Gear.GearIDRange.GetCompID(eGearComponent.Category)`, which the website writes a craftable gear's own block id into.
answer.safety: The projection is published only when every entry of that slot's policy was recognised in the game's own list. One entry the game does not carry, a slot the game has not built, or a read that throws is a whole-pool and whole-policy fallback: the game's own list is left exactly as it was built, and a fault latches the policy off until restart.
answer.noWrite: `SaveFavoritesData` and `RegisterGearInSlotAsEquipped` are never called, no data block is touched, and the favorites file is left for the game to write itself.

method: Read-only static analysis. No assembly is loaded into the CLR, no game process is started, nothing is written to a profile or to the game directory.

Method bodies were disassembled from the same `GameAssembly.dll` this file hashes (Iced x64, `il2cpp` section), and every RVA below comes from that image; `rvaSharing` counts duplicate method entries in the local `dump.cs`, where 1 is unique.
Interop member kinds, field offsets and enum constants were read from the interop assemblies listed above with Mono.Cecil.
The native read set below is pinned by `native.exact-game-reads` in `tests/NativeLayout`, so a new native member this package reads fails that audit until it is reviewed here.

hooks.name: GetAllGearForSlot
hooks.body: `GearManager.Current` → `[Current+0x30]` (= `m_gearPerSlot`) → array length check at `+0x18` → `[arr+slot*8+0x20]` where `slot` is the enum's own value (1/2/3) → `List<GearIDRange>.ToArray()`.
hooks.readback: the array the projection replaces, item by item, in the game's own order

hooks.name: OnGearLoadingDone
hooks.body: First statement is `RescanFavorites()`; then one icon task per gear; then, for each member of `InventorySlot` in reverse, `m_lastEquippedGearPerSlot` (`+0x40`), else `m_favoriteGearPerSlot` (`+0x38`)[0], else `m_gearPerSlot` (`+0x30`)[0] → `PlayerBackpackManager::EquipLocalGear`.
callers: Gear.GearManager::ParsePlayerPlayfabInventory (0x1331730), which calls it after the account inventory is stashed
hooks.readback: the three pool lists the narrowing rewrites in place, before `RescanFavorites` reads them

pool.shape: Il2CppReferenceArray<Il2CppSystem.Collections.Generic.List<Gear.GearIDRange>>, indexed by `Player.InventorySlot`'s own value; the covered slots are GearStandard 1, GearSpecial 2 and GearClass 3.

write.rule: This package writes exactly one thing in the game: the contents of the three covered lists of this pool, one item at a time, through `Clear` and `Add` on the list instances the game itself built. The list instances and the array that holds them are never replaced, so every other holder of them sees the same contents.
write.restore: The contents each slot had when this session first narrowed it are kept, and a rundown no policy is in force for — or a fault — puts them back in the same order.

pool.secondReader: Gear.GearManager::TryGetGearFromCategory (0x1333F50) reads the same pool, which is what makes the lobby's predefined-gear path (`GS_Lobby::EquipPredefinedGearForSlot`, 0x1435DB0) fail to find a category that is no longer offered.

readSet.note: Readers only. The layout audit pins this list exactly, so a new native read fails the build until it is reviewed here.

gates.notInExpedition: `GameStateManager.get_IsInExpedition()` gates the projection only: no gear can be chosen inside a level, so filtering there has no benefit and would hide a gear the player is already carrying from the in-level inventory flow. The pool is built once before any level is entered, so the loading hook is not gated on it.
gates.coveredSlots: `Player.InventorySlot` 1/2/3 only. GearMelee, HackingTool, ResourcePack and every other slot are answered with the game's own list untouched.
gates.hostOff: Plugin.Load returns before any registration or native work when the host is configured Off, so with ForgeRuntime Off this package neither reads a policy file nor installs either hook.
gates.unload: Plugin.Unload returns false, so the hooks are never removed in-process; a policy file is read once and changing it needs a restart.

authority.perClient: The pool is per-client local state built from the local data blocks and the local account inventory, and a gear choice is made locally (`CM_InventorySlotItem::PickWeapon` → `PlayerBackpackManager::EquipLocalGear`) before the synced copy is replicated. There is no host-side rejection path, so the filter is what each client applies to itself and no host validation is faked.
authority.pins: The policy's own pins — the game assembly digest, the pinned plugins and the pinned files — are read once and can only refuse the policy file that names them. They report a mismatched install; they cannot stop another machine from choosing.

limits: No claim about runtime behaviour: nothing here was executed. The two hook targets are pinned by RVA and signature, and the call edges above are literal call sites, not proof that this body ran in a game.

Whether the live pool is filled by `LoadOfflineGearDatas` (offline rows, instance text `OfflineGear_ID_<n>`) or by `ParsePlayerPlayfabInventory` (account instances), and whether the two ever both run in one process, cannot be decided statically. The projection therefore accepts either identity and refuses the whole slot when a policy entry is not recognised in the game's own list.

The saved favorites file on this machine stores `OfflineGear_ID_34` for `LastEquipped_Standard` and `OfflineGear_ID_31` for `LastEquipped_Special`, which is why the fallback a narrowed pool causes is a real path and not a theoretical one; the file itself is never written by this package.

`packetSha256` is carried by a policy for diagnostics only. It is a digest of the website's 54-slot canonical packet, and the native `pGearIDRange` has 20 component slots, so the game side cannot recompute it without a second copy of the website's encoder.
